prerequisites: Knowledge of differential calculus in one variable and basic algebra concepts

learning_outcomes.text: Will understand and be able to apply the basic concepts of calculus in one and several variables.
Will have knowledge about methods for solving differential equations and their applications in the field of industrial engineering.
Will understand the terminology, notation, and methods of Mathematics.
Will know specific software for solving mathematical problems.
Will be able to use abstraction mechanisms as a tool to help solve real-world problems.

syllabus_topics: Geometry of curves and surfaces in space
Representation of regions in the plane (Computer practices)
Differential calculus in two variables (Computer practices)
Integral calculus in two variables (Computer practices)
Solving differential equations and graphical representation of solutions (Computer practices)
assessment_rules: A minimum score of 4 out of 10 (or 2.4 out of 6) must be obtained in written tests. If this critical criterion is met, the final grade will be the weighted sum of scores from observation techniques, written tests, and practice reports/memories. If the critical criterion is not met, the final grade will be a FAIL, with the sum of all evaluation scores capped at 4.5 points. Part-time students may have non-recoverable activities substituted under specific conditions.
